limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).

Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking; a win the goldfish cannot see (`alt_win_cards`) multiplies speed's weight by 0.5.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.

DeckCheck's Threat Index is a component at prior weight 0.15 (2026-10-19): one LLM's dated read of card quality, withheld when it describes another list; its interval is a declared prior sd of 4.0 on the anchor until three decks carry two readings on one list; its score places within the bracket, its twelve rubric grades anchor.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.

The weights are a Dirichlet prior (κ = 20.0) and the inputs are drawn from their posteriors: `score` is the median of 2000 seeded draws, `score_ci` its 90% interval, and every sd in `uncertainty` is declared, not estimated.
A placement within a group of n is a (n−1)-point scale and earns the share λ = (n−1)/(n−1+4) of its component, the rest going to the cited anchor; at n=3 that is one third.
A divergent `concordance` — the deck's instruments rank it far apart — prints the grade as a range, never a letter, and the judgment must address every outlier instrument.
rank over n=3 decks; no significance claim

open_questions.question: Does the benchmark's opening-hand model include Sol Ring openers at a rate that matches real draws, and how much of the clock survives without one?
How often do the two commanders survive removal and counterspells long enough to wheel with both out? A scenario or more logged table games would answer it; the goldfish has no opponent.

findings.note: 59 vs code_score 58.9 is rounding; the argument claims no gap and names no unmeasured fact as carrying one. Nothing to attack as too-generous or too-harsh.

Both outliers (dti, resilience) are addressed: resilience by the capacity-vs-performance split with the log cutting both ways (sized by leave_one_out resilience 67.0 vs 58.9, flips not claimed); dti by a plain statement that the record does not explain its lower read, with the number at code_score. This is the second permitted answer. Rank claims (resilience 3, dti 2, speed/mana/construction 1) match concordance.instruments. No superlatives beyond rank facts.

uncertainty.method: Monte Carlo over a Dirichlet weight prior and the inputs' posteriors, joint within the group
uncertainty.priors: every sd here is declared, not estimated (docs/known-issues.md §27)

resolution: the 90% interval spans 2 grade boundaries (65, 50); concordance divergent

judgment.argument:
The measured components miss every opponent's turn. The goldfish has no blockers and no removal, so speed (kill_by_turn_8 of 0.889) is an unopposed ceiling, and the single logged game has no recorded result. I cannot show from the record that these gaps move the deck in either direction, so I sit on code_score 58.9 and round to 59.

Resilience ranks last: 11 answer cards and 1 class answered. It counts capacity to answer, and the pilot's own words agree: he had no creature or enchantment removal when the boards needed pruning. It does not count protection performance, and the pilot said Greaves and the Boots protected the commanders. That one game cannot offset a capacity gap, so the component stands and I add nothing either way.

DTI ranks second at 31 of 96. It is one dated LLM read of card quality. The record has no fact that explains why it reads lower than the goldfish does, so I do not argue with it and I do not use it to move the number.

Speed, mana and construction rank first and agree with each other. The log is the only unmeasured evidence, it is one game, and it points both ways, so this number is the measured score and not above or below it.
